conflicts.quote: Everything above is composed from shipped primitives (`Widget`, the figure cell, chips, `Refused`, the empty-state block, the route `ErrorBoundary`, `Footer`, `ArcDivider`).
conflicts.why: Two of the named pieces are not primitives this feature can compose from, so the Amendments event UX wants named at R2 is already owed. (1) The figure cell is `pages/ticker/widgets/_kit/FigureCell.tsx` — page-local to the ticker, not `shared/`. PROJECT_CONTEXT.md:136-137 binds new FE work: 'dependency direction is downward only (pages/features to shared); pages NEVER import sibling pages'. The landing cannot mount it without a `shared/` promotion whose blast radius is the desk that phases 2-3 just stabilised, with visual baselines attached. (2) The hero instrument UX's own AC-U2 requires — the dealer-gamma surface — exists nowhere in `apps/dashboard`. It is `gammaSurface()` at `design/src/lib.mjs:383-425`, and DESIGN_SYSTEM.md:138 forbids the app importing from `design/` at runtime: 'Nothing in the app imports from design/ at runtime'. (`Widget` and `Refused` ARE genuinely shared — `shared/ui/Widget/Widget.tsx`, `shared/ui/Refused.tsx` — so the assumption is half right.)
conflicts.proposal: Name the new components now rather than discovering them at build: `pages/landing/GammaSurfaceHero.tsx` (a port of the isometric projection as inline SVG — prop-free, geometry computed once at module load, `role='img'` plus an accessible name, and no `arc.ts` import so `arc.spec.ts` stays at three importers) and landing-local score/AI-read compositions fed from `pages/landing/samples.ts`. Cap them so 'one hero instrument and nothing else' stays decidable: a `?raw` set-equality scan (the proven `arc.spec.ts` pattern) asserting that the modules under `pages/landing/**` containing a `viewBox` are exactly {HeroCurve.tsx, GammaSurfaceHero.tsx}.

conflicts.quote: No element on any of the six surfaces renders a live chip, a live dot, a pulse, a beam, a particle, or the word "live" applied to itself.
conflicts.why: Marked `test` and scoped to all six surfaces, and methodology is one of the six. Methodology's job in this feature is to teach the two data clocks and to define the vocabulary — it cannot be written without the word, and neither can the landing's own field bullet that UX keeps verbatim ("The mid is tape — it pulses only while the stream is genuinely live"). "Applied to itself" is a distinction a careful reader can make and a structural check cannot. Under `[structural-over-prose-enforcement]` this becomes either a word scan that red-builds the education the BRIEF names as this feature's decision impact, or a check quietly narrowed at build time until it asserts nothing. My own AC-L5 has the same shape but is scoped to `/` only, where nothing needs the word; hers reaches the one page that does.
conflicts.proposal: Split it into two criteria. (a) No live chip, live dot, pulse, beam or particle renders on any of the six surfaces — a negative-space invariant, automate it, and prove it bites. (b) No surface in this feature describes its own displayed figures as live, current, or as-of — this is the honesty claim, it is about what a sentence means rather than which words it contains, and it is verified by review of the copy. Prose that defines what "live" means is explicitly permitted, and methodology is where it belongs.

conflicts.quote: Ruling: the landing may **state** that brokerage connect (read-only) is coming; it may not offer an action that pretends to enrol you.
conflicts.why: Read-only brokerage connect is not coming — it shipped. `features/auth/BrokerageSection.tsx` is a live Settings section that takes an app key and secret and renders connected / replace / disconnect states, and `features/trading/positions/PortfolioPanel.tsx:8,190-195` mounts a trader-visible **Broker** tab over `BrokerTabPanel`, whose header comment reads "the read-only broker surface, whose ONLY network calls are the gated `/api/broker/*` reads". The product's own shipped disclaimer already speaks in the present tense — `pages/methodology/copy.ts:12` "A connected brokerage is read-only". So this ruling cuts the enrolment control (right) while preserving a sentence the codebase contradicts (wrong), on the same screen as "Snapshot, never live". A false tense is the same class of failure as a false live dot; it is just quieter.
conflicts.proposal: Delete the sentence together with the affordance. If the landing says anything about brokerage at all, it says what is true today in the present tense (read-only, connected in Settings, never places an order). Whether it says anything is a PM/owner call — but "is coming" is not available as a wording.

conflicts.quote: **(b) Shrink to a line, keep the mechanism** — a button styled as a line action plus the existing polite in-place acknowledgement (`Landing.tsx:228,240-247`).
conflicts.why: The mechanism is the defect, not its size. The acknowledgement literal is `Landing.tsx:46` — "Thanks — we'll let you know when brokerage connect is live." It records nothing, addresses nothing, promises a message no one can send, and says "when … is live" about a capability that is already live (see my conflict on PM's P-6). Restyling the control as a line action changes the type size of the untruth, not the untruth. The a11y spec that presses `waitlist-button` (`accessibility.spec.ts:115-121`) is a reason to give that spec a new subject, not a reason to keep the subject alive.
conflicts.proposal: Delete the button, the Snackbar and the copy. Rewrite A11Y-B2 against the two CTA-band actions that survive (`Open the Ticker` primary, `Sign in` secondary) — a selector-and-subject change of the same size as (b)'s selector change, with no claim to defend afterwards.

conflicts.quote: An auth transport fault degrades to anonymous (`AuthContext`), so the wall shows; that is correct and must not become an error state.
conflicts.why: Degrading the *route decision* to anonymous is correct; degrading the *sentence* is not. With `subsystemDegraded === true` the shipped wall renders `Sign in to open {surface}` (`RequireAuth.tsx:75`) and `Private testing — invited accounts only.` (`:84`) to a trader who may well be signed in — an assertion about the visitor's identity built on a read that failed. The provider itself says the flag exists for exactly this case: `AuthContext.tsx:10-12`, "a who-am-I transport fault resolves to anonymous + sets a transient `subsystemDegraded` flag. That flag drives ONLY the gated-action "couldn't reach sign-in" copy". A route-level wall is the gated action. I am not asking for a new state peer to the wall; I am asking the wall to stop asserting a fact it does not have.
conflicts.proposal: Keep the wall as the resolution (no new route state, no error page). In the degraded branch add the shipped literal "Couldn't reach sign-in right now. Please try again in a moment." (`features/auth/copy.ts:33,46,197`) plus a Retry calling `refresh()`, and suppress the identity assertion in that branch only. AC-U29 stands as written.

conflicts.quote: It is correct today (§7.5), and a redesign that adds a skeleton to "improve" the wall would break it in a way no existing test catches.
conflicts.why: The app already does the thing this forbids, two routes away and on the identical fact: `app.tsx:127-131`'s `DefaultTickerRedirect` renders `<RouteFallback />` while `!ready`, with the comment "Waits for the ONE non-blocking who-am-I read (`ready`) behind the quiet route fill". So a quiet fill on `!ready` is this codebase's own established answer, not an improvement someone invented. `null` is not a hold a person can perceive: on a hard load of `/scanner` a signed-in trader gets an empty region under a mounted nav with nothing saying anything is happening — which is precisely what PM's AC-A3 forbids ("it never leaves the visitor on an indefinite blank"). What must not ship is a *signed-out-looking* placeholder; a neutral fill that makes no auth claim is not one.
conflicts.proposal: While `!ready`, render the same `RouteFallback` the redirect already uses — not the wall, not a skeleton *of* the wall, not `null`. AC-U28 stands: "never the wall, never `null`."

conflicts.quote: Mitigation: a **component-level** `React.lazy` boundary for the field section only, inside the still-eager Landing.
conflicts.why: That creates a loading state in the middle of the acquisition page — the one state my matrix declares n/a-by-construction, and the one state no copy exists for. A Suspense fallback there resolves to one of three bad things: a spinner (a second moving element on a page whose motion budget is the hero draw), a skeleton shimmer (a data-signal keyframe, which fails canon's Motion predicate (a) because there is no stream to gate it), or a zero-height box (layout shift directly under the H1 on first paint). The bundle argument is real; the unstated state is mine to answer before the boundary lands, not after.
conflicts.proposal: If the boundary lands, its fallback is a reserved-height quiet panel carrying the section's own `Structure field` title and the sample footnote — no spinner, no shimmer, no height collapse — and the landing gains a `loading` row in the state matrix that I will write. If that fallback is unacceptable, import the field eagerly and pay the bytes.

conflicts.quote: Ruling: either the table is complete, or it says in one clause that it is a selection.
conflicts.why: Canon rule 24 is not a list this page may sample: "**nine members** … Distinct literals, never synonyms; rendered as Sans text, never as a figure; a **tenth** member is an **Amendments** event" (`DESIGN_SYSTEM.md:179`). A "this is a selection" clause on the one page that defines the closed vocabulary teaches the trader that the set is open — the exact inversion the rule exists to prevent, and the reason the canon was widened from six to nine on 2026-09-03. The architect reached nine independently (§4.5). Separately, neither position addresses the second half of rule 24: `methodology.mjs:60` renders every literal `class="mono"`, i.e. in the figure register, which the rule forbids.
conflicts.proposal: Nine rows, nine distinct definitions, no synonyms, pinned by set-equality to the canon's members so a tenth red-builds the page that documents it; every literal rendered Sans, never mono, never as a figure. AC-U20 stands; delete the "selection" escape hatch.

conflicts.quote: `/methodology` names no product surface a visitor cannot reach from the running app — in particular it contains no pointer to a "what's sent" screen.

Reserve the cut for `persona`, `flows` and `operator`, which genuinely are documentation.

conflicts.quote: | **AC-L11** | S7 | With JavaScript disabled, loading `/` shows a readable line naming Convexa and a working link to a document that renders without JavaScript. Today it shows a blank page. | review |
conflicts.why: I accept the defect and want the fix; the mark is wrong and the mark is my column. A `<noscript>` block is invisible in every normal pass — nobody reviews the acquisition page with JavaScript off — so its silent removal by any future build or template change is unobservable. That is the textbook `test` side of `spire-tech-risk-based-verify` (invariant, negative space, silently regressing) and the opposite of the `review` side (visible, intentional copy). Marked `review`, this criterion is checked exactly once, at build, and never again.
conflicts.proposal: `Verify by: test` — assert the served `index.html` contains a `<noscript>` whose text names Convexa and whose link resolves to a document that renders without the module bundle. The copy inside it is mine to write.

conflicts.quote: AC-M2 is `review` deliberately: the fact being checked is agreement between a sentence and an engine constant, and `apps/api` is frozen this phase — an automated cross-check would either import the backend or assert a hard-coded number against another hard-coded number, which proves nothing.
conflicts.why: Then the page must not assert the numbers. `40 / 25 / 25 / 10 / 6` on a public methodology page is five claims with no vouching mechanism the moment the reviewer walks away; the architect names the same gap and files it as debt (his risk 6), and PM's own risk 4 says this page is where this feature can do real harm. "Frozen this phase" is not the horizon that matters — `[score-change-is-deliberate-and-measured]` explicitly contemplates the score moving. And the third option is available: a test does not have to import the backend, it can read the engine source from disk the way this repo's `?raw` source scans already read app source, and fail when a constant moves. This is the same refusal I made against "69 tracked names" in my own R1; I cannot apply it to the landing and waive it on the trust page.
conflicts.proposal: Keep `review` for the wording of the section, and add one `test` that reads the engine's score constants from source and asserts the table's caps equal them, with a mutation proof. If that mechanism is refused, drop the Max column and state each component without a number (the architect's own §4.6 fallback). I will not sign copy that asserts five engine constants nothing checks.
